title: HOSA Nutrition: Carbohydrates, Proteins, and Fats - HOSA Nutrition - Macronutrients: Nitrogen Balance Calculation
exam: HOSA Nutrition: Carbohydrates, Proteins, and Fats
subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: A patient consumes 75g of protein in a day and excretes 10g of nitrogen in their urine. Assuming a constant factor of 4g nitrogen loss for non-urinary routes is *not* used in this simplified clinical estimate (using Nitrogen Intake vs Output + 4 is common, but basic clinical check often uses Intake/6.25 - UUN - 4). Let's use the standard Nitrogen Balance formula: $N_{balance} = N_{intake} - (N_{urine} + 4)$. Calculate the nitrogen balance.
questions.explain: Step 1: Calculate $N_{intake}$. Protein is $\approx 16\%$ nitrogen, so divide protein by 6.25. $75\text{g} / 6.25 = 12\text{g Nitrogen}$. Step 2: Formula $12 - (10 + 4) = 12 - 14 = -2$. The patient is in negative nitrogen balance (catabolic).
